subject: SOC2 / SIG / CAIQ — subprocessor retention, onboarding windows and crypto handling (NovaMed)

Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novamed.com>
Date: Thu, 08 Jan 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: NovaMed SOC2 packet — updated subprocessor roster + retention windows

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our SOC2 renewal we need an updated subprocessor roster and a concise mapping of retention windows (how long NovaMed customer data is retained by each subprocessor) for the SIG/CAIQ review. Specifically we need: 

- A single CSV with: vendor name, purpose, data types processed, contract start date, retention period (in days), region of processing, and encryption at rest? Y/N.
- Any onboarding SLAs for adding new subprocessors (how far in advance do you notify; what evidence is available).
- A brief note on key management for vendors that store encrypted customer data (who holds keys; KMS/HSM provider).

Can you provide this by EOD next Tuesday (Jan 13)? We're also interested in whether you offer a contractual subprocessor notification window (e.g., 30 days) or a physical manifest we can pull during audits.

Attachment: NovaMed_SIG_Request_20260105.pdf (PDF, 85KB)

Appreciate it — Tom

--
Tom Evans
Security & Compliance Manager
NovaMed Health

Subject: Re: NovaMed SOC2 packet — updated subprocessor roster + retention windows

Tom — thanks for the clear ask. We're putting together a single CSV and an evidence bundle. To make sure we hit the right scope I have two quick clarifying questions: 

1) For "retention period" do you want the retention policy Redwood enforces for customer data (our default), or the retention period that applies to each subprocessor independently (e.g., logs retained 90 days at ProcLog)? We can provide both columns.
2) For key management: do you need a vendor-by-vendor KMS owner mapping, or a summary (e.g., "Redwood-managed keys in AWS KMS; select subprocessors use their own KMS")?

We plan to deliver a CSV (redwood_subprocessors_v2.csv) and an evidence ZIP with excerpts of contracts, KMS mapping, and the onboarding checklist. Marissa will add the onboarding SLA language.

Attachment: redwood_subprocessors_v2.csv (CSV, 12KB)

I'll send a fuller package early next week.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2026 09:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: NovaMed SOC2 packet — updated subprocessor roster + retention windows

Tom / Jasmine — adding the onboarding & retention details here so the CSV is self-contained. Inline summary to include with the CSV: 

Onboarding windows & notification
- Notice: Redwood provides contractual notice for new subprocessors where feasible. Standard window is 30 days for major data processors; 10 business days for low-risk utility providers.
- Evidence: onboarding package includes SOC2 or ISO attestation, security questionnaire, and KMS ownership statement (where applicable).
- Emergency additions: in rare cases (critical cloud provider fixes), we may add an emergency subprocessor with post-hoc notification and compensating controls documented.

Retention mapping (examples)
- Logging provider "ProcLog": logs retained 90 days by default; NovaMed-data tokens masked at source; encrypted at rest (AWS KMS).
- Analytics "Metricly": aggregated telemetry retained 365 days; raw PII not stored.

Key management (high-level)
- Redwood uses customer-scoped KMS keys for production workloads when customers enable KMS; otherwise, Redwood-managed keys in AWS KMS with separation of duties.
- For subprocessors that store customer data encrypted at rest, we provide a vendor KMS owner column in the CSV; we can also export a KMS mapping sheet for auditors.

If you want contract excerpts instead of summaries, we can include 1-page redactions per vendor.

Marissa Cole
Head of Trust & Security Operations

From: Tom Evans <tevans@novamed.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@novamed.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2026 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: NovaMed SOC2 packet — updated subprocessor roster + retention windows

Thanks — that's very helpful. A couple of clarifying asks before we close the ticket:

- Can you confirm whether Redwood will provide a machine-readable manifest (CSV) that includes an ISO 8601 "vendor_effective_date" for each subprocessor and a boolean field "handles_customer_keys"? We use those fields to automate our vendor churn checks.
- Oncrypto: for vendors that store encrypted PHI, do any subprocessors hold customer-managed keys directly (i.e., customer directly provisions keys to the vendor KMS)? If yes, please list which vendors and the model.

Also — our procurement team asked if you can provide contractual language that commits to a 30-day notification for material subprocessor changes. If Redwood cannot offer that uniformly, please indicate which vendor classes it's limited to.

Would appreciate the machine-readable CSV and KMS mapping by EOD Monday (Jan 12).

Cheers,
Tom

If you want a signed contractual addendum for the 30-day notification for material changes, we can loop Legal and Procurement (Ben is copied) and push a simple rider.
